record.paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
record.context_brief: refined symmetry away from small set
record.original_question: Let (X, d, p) be a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit obtained as a Gromov–Hausdorff limit of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For each k ≤ n − 2, does there exist a subset Ŝ^k of Hausdorff dimension at most k such that every point x ∈ X \ Ŝ^k has the property that every tangent cone at x is at least (k+1)-symmetric, meaning it splits off at least k+1 Euclidean factors?

evidence.quote: We say X is k-symmetric if X ≡ Rk × C(Y ) additionally splits off k-Euclidean factors.

Conjecture 2.16. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then for each k ≤ n − 2 there exists Ŝk with dim Ŝk ≤ k such that for each x ∈ X \ Ŝk we have that every tangent cone is at least k + 1-symmetric.

artifact.category_tag: Ricci limit spaces and singular sets
artifact.status_search_result: The standard stratification result of Cheeger–Colding (with rectifiability by Cheeger–Jiang–Naber, Annals 2021) gives that the singular stratum $S^k$, defined as points where no tangent cone is $(k+1)$-symmetric, has Hausdorff dimension at most $k$. The stronger refined statement asking for a set $\hat S^k$ of dimension at most $k$ off which every tangent cone (not merely one) is $(k+1)$-symmetric does not appear to be established in the literature; tangent cones at a fixed point need not be unique, and no published resolution of this refined symmetry conjecture in the noncollapsed setting was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Rectifiability of singular sets of noncollapsed limit spaces with Ricci curvature bounded below
status_evidence.snippet: Cheeger–Jiang–Naber prove rectifiability of the standard singular strata $S^k$ in noncollapsed Ricci limits, giving dim $S^k\le k$ and $k$-rectifiability.
status_evidence.claim: The classical strata satisfy dim $S^k\le k$, but the refined statement that every tangent cone is $(k+1)$-symmetric off a set of dimension $\le k$ is not established here.

status_evidence.title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the refined symmetry statement as a conjecture for noncollapsed Ricci limits.
status_evidence.claim: The refined symmetry conjecture is recorded as an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$, $\lambda\ge 0$, and $v>0$ be fixed constants. Suppose $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ is a sequence of pointed complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds satisfying
$$\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}\ge -\lambda \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{Vol}\bigl(B_1(p_i)\bigr)>v,$$
and that $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space $(X,d,p)$ (a noncollapsed lower Ricci limit space).

For a point $x\in X$, a tangent cone at $x$ is any pointed Gromov–Hausdorff limit $(T_xX,d_x,x_*)$ of a rescaled sequence $(X,r_j^{-1}d,x)$ with $r_j\downarrow 0$. A metric space $Z$ is called $\ell$-symmetric if it is isometric to a product $\mathbb{R}^\ell \times C(Y)$ where $C(Y)$ denotes a metric cone over some metric space $Y$.

Question: For every integer $k$ with $0\le k\le n-2$, does there exist a Borel subset $\hat S^k\subseteq X$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_{\mathcal H}\hat S^k\le k$ such that for every point $x\in X\setminus \hat S^k$, every tangent cone at $x$ is at least $(k+1)$-symmetric?
